about: Claims ruled on by professional fact-checking desks (Google fact-check index, ClaimReview), reviewed since 2024-10-01; the label is the desk's published rating, with the ruling's link and date. Built by eval/buildRulingSuite.js --queries world --out rulings_pool2 --prefix rp2 --caps true=80,misleading=0,false=same on 2026-10-29. Run with FACT_CHECK_CHANNEL=off as well: with the channel on it finds the very ruling a case is labelled from. Relabelled 2026-10-29 (eval/buildRulingSuite.js --relabel): {"true->false":8}.

Ukrainian Drone Damaged Portuguese F-16s at Estonian Air Base

ruling.rating: No such incident occurred. Neither NATO nor Estonia reported any airspace violation on August 6, any drone shootdown, or any damage to aircraft. The site hosting the "story" is a clone of The Defense Post, and the footage of burning wreckage in the video was generated by artificial intelligence and spliced into a genuine NATO video report.

cases.input: France's Army Would Last Just Seven Days Against Russia, Statista Says

ruling.rating: Neither Statista nor the Institute for the Study of War published any such study. The infographic circulating online is a forgery built on Statista's visual branding. The real debate about France's insufficient stockpiles of certain types of ammunition does not mean the country would be defeated by Russia in seven days.
